4738575ced46c35d87c56b79fc130afada0b2222.summary: IBM Security X-Force describes Minodo, a backdoor loaded by the Dave Loader crypter since late February 2023. X-Force assesses its developers were linked to ITG14 (FIN7), and that former Trickbot/Conti (ITG23) members use it to deliver the Project Nemesis infostealer or Cobalt Strike. The report notes code overlap with the Lizar malware family. Attribution is hedged as assessment or likelihood.

hedges: The report says it was republished with the family renamed from Domino to Minodo to avoid confusion with the HCL Domino brand, and that the malware is unrelated to HCL.
X-Force assesses the Minodo malware was created by developers associated with ITG14, and suspects it was created by current or former ITG14 developers.
Former ITG23 members are likely behind recent Dave Loader campaigns and probably collaborated with current or former ITG14 developers.
The report says C2 address overlap with ITG14 infrastructure is insufficient for attribution but is consistent with other evidence.
Attribution of the Dave-loaded Cobalt Strike samples to Royal is described as suspected.
X-Force assesses that infostealers may often be deployed during lower priority infections.
X-Force assesses that ITG14 members responsible for developing Minodo probably had a relationship with Project Nemesis.

477096318b2545e6e1330383ccf77393d2a4378b.summary: SecurityScorecard assesses with moderate confidence that the DarkSide ransomware group, also known as Carbon Spider, was responsible for the May 2021 ransomware attack on Colonial Pipeline. The report says over 80GB of data was exfiltrated, likely for extortion. The FBI had earlier stated DarkSide was responsible. SecurityScorecard found no evidence of direct disruption to Colonial's critical infrastructure, though damage elsewhere in its network is plausible. The report also lists other suspected victims identified through network flow analysis. It says its analysis was ongoing and that…

hedges: Through an ongoing investigation, SecurityScorecard has found with a moderate confidence level that the DarkSide ransomware group is responsible.
Attribution is often difficult and requires much analysis to attribute any cyber-attack to a specific group with any degree of certainty.
It is plausible that Carbon Spider caused damage to other parts of the Colonial Pipeline network, though no direct disruption was found.
The Analysis of Competing Hypotheses is marked as in progress.
NetFlow data does not include content, so the report was unable to view the data exfiltrated.
The report suspects some IP addresses were used by attackers reviewing and downloading the data, and that proxies may have been used.
The attribution analysis was based on publicly available clearweb and open access dark web sources.
